text: A bathroom fitter can hang a vanity over newly tiled walls and still true the door line, because the in-out travel takes up the variation in tile bed thickness.
A hire fleet can cable-tie one to each spare wheel well, so a driver has the right four sizes without a socket set in the cab
A picture framer can cut a replacement pane for a frame from a stock sheet, scoring on the bench and snapping it on the edge with the tapping head.
A garage can clean up the thread on a sump plug or a bracket before refitting, so a damaged thread does not mean a new part.
A tool hire counter can list the gun as a kit, since the battery and charger travel with the tool and the tube is the only item left to supply.
A body shop can trim a repair panel along a curve on the car, where a grinder would burn the paint and leave a burr to dress back.
A 43 cm gun with a 230 mm hose reaches nipples on a machine parked against a wall, so nothing has to be moved out of the bay
A hire fleet can pack a bottle with each tool, so an operator oils it at the start of a shift instead of the workshop finding a dry tool at service.
A shopfitter can hold a service access panel in a reception desk closed, since the magnet releases with a light pull and leaves the face unbroken
A bathroom showroom can hold one clamp for every shelf thickness on display, so a replacement part comes off the shelf without a size question.
A shopfitter can fit a set to a mobile display stand that is wheeled between events, so the unit rolls quietly across a polished floor instead of being carried.
A picture framer or model maker can score a short tube over a bench edge and snap it, so leftover lengths are used instead of binned
A gas engineer can break a union behind a boiler where a rigid wrench will not swing, so a service does not turn into a casing removal.
A car body restorer can trim a patch panel to a curve on the bench, where a grinder would leave a burr to file back
A sign installer can set threaded inserts into a hollow aluminium post on site, where there is no access to the back of the section.
A maintenance fitter can take the machine up a stairwell and drill fixings for a handrail without finding a socket outlet on the landing.
A duct fabricator can set inserts along a run of duct for access hatches, so each hatch is fixed to threaded points rather than self-tapping screws.
A hotel refurbishment can have vanity tops re-polished in place between room handovers, with the water-fed head keeping dust off the soft furnishings.
A maintenance team can carry one lock reference for every sliding window on a block, so a broken catch is replaced on the first visit
A balcony door set can be assembled with the hook lock in place and shipped as one unit, so the site fitter hangs a finished sash rather than a bare frame.
A student hall can fit one rail per bedroom wall, so each room has hanging space without a wardrobe being installed
A landscaper can trim a coping stone or a paving edge with a mallet where a saw will not fit, so the piece is dressed on site.
A hardware retailer can hang the pack as a single-size line, so a customer buying hinge screws finds the pilot bit beside them
A stone walling contractor can dress a quoin or a lintel on the ground before it is lifted, so the block goes into the wall at the right size.
A landlord can have a rental flat's walls and ceilings sanded between tenancies in one visit, since one operator covers both without a tower
